title: Perspective-driven reranker evals: NDCG/MRR telemetry + live A/B hooks
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Improve reranking quality observability and safe rollout mechanics by instrumenting per-perspective NDCG/MRR, adding stratified customer-promptset slices, and exposing light-weight A/B hooks for canarying new reranker configs. This ticket covers telemetry schema changes, sampling rules for live traffic, offline/online comparison pipelines, and the initial rollout plan for a low-risk canary.
acceptance_criteria: NDGC@5 and MRR@10 computed and emitted per-request with tags: customer_id, prompt_set_id, query_type, perspective (candidate-origin)
Dashboard with stratified views (customer slices, query_type, latency buckets) is available in Grafana and documented in Confluence
Live A/B hook implemented: 5% canary traffic routing + deterministic seeding and automatic rollback signal when relative NDCG drop > 3% or p95 latency increase > 30%
Offline k-fold eval matches live telemetry within +/-2pp on representative holdout for three customer slices
Open PR for runtime changes merged and end-to-end test coverage added for telemetry tags and AB-routing logic
tasks: Define 'perspective' taxonomy and mapping for candidate provenance (embedding-source, model-variant, user-history)
Schema update: add ndcg@k, mrr@k, baseline_model tag to event proto and DB export
Instrument rerank endpoint to compute ground-truth metrics for logged queries using stored relevance labels or synthetic heuristics
Build Grafana panels and CSV export for downstream analysis
Implement AB hook: routing policy config, canary sampling, deterministic hashing, rollback detectors
Create PRD and share with PM + Design for visibility; schedule review with Reliability
decisions: Use NDCG@5 and MRR@10 as primary quality signals — they balance short-list quality and early ranks for downstream UX
Compute metrics in the service synchronously for sampled requests (1% by default) to get low-latency telemetry; bulk backfill from logged requests for higher sample rates offline
Tagging approach: lightweight string tags (customer_id, prompt_set_id, query_type, perspective) to avoid schema churn in dashboards
Rollback thresholds: relative NDCG drop > 3% OR absolute MRR drop of 0.02 combined with p95 latency increase > 30% triggers automated rollback for canary
Start with 5% canary traffic, scaling to 25% after 24h with no regression signals
notes: Initial offline eval on customer-slice A (100k queries) shows +1.8pp NDCG@5 for candidate reweighting with negligible latency change
We observed a small telemetry skew between synchronous on-service metrics and batch backfill (0.7pp). Plan: normalize by applying the same tokenization and candidate filtering in the backfill job
Reliability requested a guard for memory usage when computing metrics synchronously — implemented histogram-based bounded scorer to prevent OOMs
PM asked for a human-review window before automated rollback on enterprise customers — added allowlist for manual holdouts
